title: The build identity names the source revision it was built from
outcome: The build identity names the source revision it was built from
acceptance: The build components that `engram doctor --json` and `engram readiness --json` print gain a source revision field: the commit id of the tree the executable was built from, a marker when that tree had uncommitted changes, and an explicit unavailable value when the build could not determine it; a test asserts the field's presence and shape

Building outside a Git checkout, or without Git installed, still succeeds and reports the revision as unavailable; the build script change is covered by a test or by a documented manual check recorded in the item's notes with its command output
The backup manifest's source revision field is filled from this value, and a test asserts that the manifest carries the same revision the build reports
docs/features/cli-and-mcp.md's build identity section describes the field and says it is recovery information, not proof that the revision rebuilds to the same binary

completion.summary: The build identity names its source revision. A build script records `<commit>`, `<commit>+dirty` or `unavailable`, read-only and failing soft. The value is a fingerprinted build component printed by doctor, readiness and next. `--version` shows `rev <12>[+dirty]`, and the backup manifest records it. The docs describe it as recovery information. Landed as 4c6a92d; the installed build is 7e42ebb769cd and reports rev 4c6a92d362a3.
